operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The President says "hereby appoint Benjamin W." Thoron (the surname is on the next printed line) as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice Guy J. Swope, resigned, to serve without additional compensation and to exercise the functions conferred by EOs 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689, and amends those orders accordingly. The appointment and amendment are one-time acts performed on signing, December 4, 1942; the order states no effective date and has no term. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 the appointing act is recorded as exhausted by performance and the surviving appointment is treated as a consequence. EO 9618 (1945-09-19) names a successor 'vice Benjamin W. Thoron, resigned', so Thoron's service ended by resignation between 1942-12-04 and 1945-09-19; the exact resignation date is not held and is not needed for the first end of the order's own command.

later_events.mechanism: EO 9618 appoints Edwin G. Arnold as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration vice Benjamin W. Thoron, resigned (a successor appointment that recites the end of Thoron's service; not a revocation or supersession of EO 9278)

research_rationale:
EO 9278 (signed December 4, 1942; F.R. Doc. 42-12921, filed December 5, 1942) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and the act of February 11, 1936 the President appoints Benjamin W. Thoron, Director, Division of Territories and Island Possessions, Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice Guy J. Swope, resigned, to serve without additional compensation and to exercise the functions conferred on the Administration and Administrator by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, and amends those orders accordingly. The order is a one-time appointment and amendment, complete when issued on 1942-12-04; Thoron's later service is a historical consequence of the appointment, and the functions he exercised are conferred by the earlier orders, which keep their own lifecycles. A later order, EO 9618 (September 19, 1945), appoints a successor 'vice Benjamin W. Thoron, resigned', showing the service had ended by resignation on a date before then that no held source gives; that is recorded as a later event, not an end. Applying the owner ruling of 2026-10-28, the appointing act is recorded as exhausted by performance and the surviving appointment is separated from it. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

It is a one-time command performed that day, so the order is exhausted by performance on 1943-03-03 and the designation stays revoked as a surviving consequence. The order has no sunset, report or continuing duty.

research_rationale:
EO 9314 (signed March 15, 1943; F.R. Doc. 43-4093, filed March 16, 1943) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Under Title II of the act of November 26, 1940, on the recommendation of the Civil Service Commission, it revokes EO 8955 of December 1, 1941 (which extended the Classification Act of 1923 to certain War and Navy Department positions and set a salary differential) and provides that the order takes effect as of March 15, 1943. The held text continues with a Civil Service Commission regulation after the filing line; that is another document and was not used. All three scopes are performed together on 1943-03-15 and are exhausted by performance; the revocation of EO 8955 stays in place as a surviving consequence. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

The machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage (all three marked complete, no scope note) and are recorded as leads, not as independent review. The order's own effective-date item fixes the date, 1943-03-15; nothing shows an earlier end or a postponement.","independent_command_check":"No independent command: item 1 revokes EO 8955 and item 2 fixes when that happens. FEDERALREGISTER
VOLUME 1 0 1 9 3 4* ^A/ITED 7 NUMBER 197
Washington , Saturday , October 6, 1945
The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9638
Creating  the  C ivilian  P roduction  A d­
ministration  and T erminating  the  W ar
P roduction  B oard
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and Statutes, includ­
ing Title I of the First War Powers Act* 
1941, and as President of the United 
States, it is ordered as follows:
1 . All functions and powers of the War 
Production Board, established by Execu­
tive Order No. 9024 of January 16, 1942, 
and ah agencies, officers (other than the 
Chairman and the other members of the 
War Production Board) . employees, rec­
ords, property, and funds of the Board, 
are transferred to a Civilian Production 
Administration which is hereby estab­
lished in the Office for Emergency Man­
agement of the Executive Office of the 
President. , The War Production Board 
is hereby terminated.
2. At the head of the Civilian Produc­
tion Administration (hereinafter referred 
to as the Administration) there shall 
be a Civilian Production Administrator 
(hereinafter referred to as the Adminis­
trator) who shall be appointed by the 
President and receive a salary of $12,000 
per annum, unless the Congress shall, 
otherwise provide, together with actual 
and necessary transportation, subsist­
ence, and other expenses incidental to 
the performance of his duties. All the 
functions and powers vested in the 
Chairman of the War Production Board 
on the effective date of this order are 
transferred to the Civilian Production 
Administrator and may be performed 
by him through such officials, persons, or 
agencies as he shall determine. The Ad­
ministrator shall exercise his functions 
and powers in accordance with the gen­
eral policies established by the Director 
of War Mobilization and Reconversion.
3. The functions and powers trans­
ferred by this order shall, to the extent 
authorized by law, be utilized to further 
a swift and orderly transition from war­
time production to a maximum peace­
time production in industry free from 
wartime Government controls, with due
regard for the stability of prices and 
costs; and to that end shall be utilized 
to: (a) expand the production of mate­
rials which are in short supply, (b) limit 
the manufacture of products for which 
materials or facilities are insufficient,
(c) control the accumulation of inven­
tories so as to avoid speculative hoarding 
and unbalanced distribution which would 
curtail total production, (d) grant pri­
ority assistance to break bottlenecks 
which would impede the reconversion 
process, (e) facilitate the fulfillment of 
relief and other essential export pro­
grams, and (f) allocate scarce materials 
and facilities necessary for the produc­
tion of low-priced items essential to the 
continued success of the stabilization 
program of the Federal Government.
4. The Administrator may, to the ex­
tent authorized by law, terminate any 
function vested in the Administration by 
this order when he shall deem such action 
to be in the national interest. The Ad­
ministrator shall be responsible for the 
orderly liquidation of all affairs relating 
to any function so terminated and shall 
also from time to time take all appro­
priate steps looking toward the liquida­
tion of the Administration.
5. Such further measures and disposi­
tions as may be determined by the Direc­
tor of the Bureau of the Budget to be 
necessary to effectuate the transfers and 
terminations provided for in this order 
shall be carried out in such manner as 
the Director may direct and by such 
agencies as he may designate.
6. All prior regulations, orders, rulings, 
directives and other actions relating to 
any function transferred by this order 
shall remain in effect except insofar as 
they are in conflict with this order or 
are hereafter amended under proper au­
thority.
7. All provisions of prior Executive 
Orders which are in conflict with this 
order are amended accordingly.
8. This order shall be effective as of 
the close of business on the third day of 
November, 1945.
H arry S. T ruman
T he  W hite  H ouse ,
October 4, 1945.
[F. R. Doc. 45-18515; Filed, Oct. 4, 1945;
3:38 p. m.]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Paragraph 1 of Executive Order 9024 is amended to include three more officers as members of the War Production Board. The clause continues, amended, as long as the Board exists (owner ruling 2026-10-21, strike-and-insert). EO 9638 sec. 1 says the Civilian Production Administration is established and "is hereby terminated" applies to the War Production Board (the sentence 'The War Production Board is hereby terminated.' is printed across two lines), and sec. 8 makes the order effective as of "the close of business on the third day of" November, 1945. The Board, and with it the clause enlarging its membership, therefore ended on 1945-11-03 (inclusive; the exclusive reading is that it ended as that day closed, the same instant). The amendment recorded before and after: before, the Board's membership under paragraph 1 of EO 9024 did not name these three officers; after, it did, until the Board ended.

research_rationale:
EO 9335 (signed April 19, 1943) was read in full in the registered held text, the pdfplumber recheck of the Federal Register page (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9335.recheck.txt, 8 FR 5425, grade original_representation_unverified; reading-order text rebuilt from the scan's OCR word positions; page images were not compared). It amends paragraph 1 of EO 9024 of January 16, 1942, as amended, to add the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission, the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation and the Petroleum Administrator for War as members of the War Production Board. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, until its parent ends. The parent body ended when EO 9638 (signed October 4, 1945; 10 FR 12591) terminated the War Production Board effective as of the close of business on November 3, 1945, so the membership clause ended with the Board on 1945-11-03. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9638
Creating  the  C ivilian  P roduction  A d­
ministration  and T erminating  the  W ar

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and Statutes, includ­
ing Title I of the First War Powers Act* 
1941, and as President of the United 
States, it is ordered as follows:
1 . All functions and powers of the War 
Production Board, established by Execu­
tive Order No. 9024 of January 16, 1942, 
and ah agencies, officers (other than the 
Chairman and the other members of the 
War Production Board) . employees, rec­
ords, property, and funds of the Board, 
are transferred to a Civilian Production 
Administration which is hereby estab­
lished in the Office for Emergency Man­
agement of the Executive Office of the 
President. , The War Production Board 
is hereby terminated.
2. At the head of the Civilian Produc­
tion Administration (hereinafter referred 
to as the Administration) there shall 
be a Civilian Production Administrator 
(hereinafter referred to as the Adminis­
trator) who shall be appointed by the 
President and receive a salary of $12,000 
per annum, unless the Congress shall, 
otherwise provide, together with actual 
and necessary transportation, subsist­
ence, and other expenses incidental to 
the performance of his duties. All the 
functions and powers vested in the 
Chairman of the War Production Board 
on the effective date of this order are 
transferred to the Civilian Production 
Administrator and may be performed 
by him through such officials, persons, or 
agencies as he shall determine. The Ad­
ministrator shall exercise his functions 
and powers in accordance with the gen­
eral policies established by the Director 
of War Mobilization and Reconversion.
3. The functions and powers trans­
ferred by this order shall, to the extent 
authorized by law, be utilized to further 
a swift and orderly transition from war­
time production to a maximum peace­
time production in industry free from 
wartime Government controls, with due
regard for the stability of prices and 
costs; and to that end shall be utilized 
to: (a) expand the production of mate­
rials which are in short supply, (b) limit 
the manufacture of products for which 
materials or facilities are insufficient,
(c) control the accumulation of inven­
tories so as to avoid speculative hoarding 
and unbalanced distribution which would 
curtail total production, (d) grant pri­
ority assistance to break bottlenecks 
which would impede the reconversion 
process, (e) facilitate the fulfillment of 
relief and other essential export pro­
grams, and (f) allocate scarce materials 
and facilities necessary for the produc­
tion of low-priced items essential to the 
continued success of the stabilization 
program of the Federal Government.
4. The Administrator may, to the ex­
tent authorized by law, terminate any 
function vested in the Administration by 
this order when he shall deem such action 
to be in the national interest. The Ad­
ministrator shall be responsible for the 
orderly liquidation of all affairs relating 
to any function so terminated and shall 
also from time to time take all appro­
priate steps looking toward the liquida­
tion of the Administration.
5. Such further measures and disposi­
tions as may be determined by the Direc­
tor of the Bureau of the Budget to be 
necessary to effectuate the transfers and 
terminations provided for in this order 
shall be carried out in such manner as 
the Director may direct and by such 
agencies as he may designate.
6. All prior regulations, orders, rulings, 
directives and other actions relating to 
any function transferred by this order 
shall remain in effect except insofar as 
they are in conflict with this order or 
are hereafter amended under proper au­
thority.
7. All provisions of prior Executive 
Orders which are in conflict with this 
order are amended accordingly.
8. This order shall be effective as of 
the close of business on the third day of 
November, 1945.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: item 1: Paragraph 1 of Executive Order No. 9139 is amended to read as a new paragraph establishing the War Manpower Commission within the Office for Emergency Management and fixing who its members are. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 the restatement continues, amended, until the parent ends. EO 9617 section 1(c) says "is hereby terminated" of the War Manpower Commission (printed 'The War Manpower Commission' at the end of one line and the verb phrase on the next), with no effective-date wording, so the Commission and its composition clause ended on signing, September 19, 1945. Before and after: before the amendment paragraph 1 described an earlier membership; after it, the restated membership applied until the Commission ended. The substance of the paragraph changed (a whole-paragraph rewrite).

research_rationale:
EO 9409 (signed December 23, 1943; F.R. Doc. 43-20397, filed December 24, 1943) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Item 1 restates, by amendment, paragraph 1 of EO 9139 of April 18, 1942 to set the composition of the War Manpower Commission; item 2 revokes paragraph 1 of EO 9279 of December 5, 1942. The held text goes on to print EO 9410 (delegation of Selective Service functions) and a contents page; they are other orders and were not used. Item 2 is a one-time revocation performed on signing, 1943-12-23. Item 1 is a strike-and-insert restatement that, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21, continues until its parent ends; the Commission ended when EO 9617 (signed September 19, 1945; 10 FR 11929) section 1(c) terminated it, with no effective-date wording, so on 1945-09-19. The whole-order end is the later date, 1945-09-19. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

The EO 9410 text on the same page cites 'Executive Order No. 9379 of December 5, 1942' for paragraphs 2(a) to 2(c); that is EO 9279 (December 5, 1942) misprinted, not this order, and it concerns Selective Service functions, so it is not an event for EO 9409. By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and the statutes, 
including Title I of the First War Powers 
Act, 1941, and as President of the United 
States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1 , (a) Except as otherwise provided 
herein, all functions, agencies, officers, 
employees, records, property, and funds 
of the War Manpower Commission, es­
tablished by Executive Order 9139 of 
April 18, 1942, are hereby transferred to 
the Department of Labor and shall be 
administered under the supervision, di­
rection, and control of the Secretary of 
Labor.
(b) All of the functions of the Chair­
man of the War Manpower Commission, 
exclusive of so much thereof as relates 
to the functions of the Procurement and 
Assignment Service transferred by para­
graph 5 of this order, are transferred to 
the Secretary of Labor.
(c) The War Manpower Commission 
is hereby terminated.
(d) In order to maintain the essential 
coordination of public employment serv­
ice and unemployment compensation 
functions and to avoid any necessity for 
establishing duplicate public employ­
ment office facilities, the Department of 
Labor is directed to provide for making 
available to agencies charged with the 
administration of unemployment com­
pensation laws such services, informa­
tion, and facilities by the United States 
Employment Service as the Secretary of 
Labor shall find not inconsistent with 
the purposes of this order. To the extent 
that Federal funds under the jurisdiction 
of the Social Security Board are involved 
in the effectuation of this section, serv­
ices, information, and facilities shall be 
furnished only when, and to the extent 
that the Social Security Board shall 
approve.
2. (a) The National War Labor Board, 
established by Executive Order 9017 of 
January 12, 1942, and all of its func­
tions, officers, employees, records, prop­
erty, and funds are hereby transferred
to the Department of Labor and shall, 
except as otherwise provided in this or­
der, be administered under the super­
vision, direction, and control of the Sec­
retary of Labor.
(b) The National War Labor Board in 
the Department of Labor shall be in all 
respects subject to and governed by such 
policies, consistent with law, as the Sec­
retary of Labor shall prescribe; and so 
much of the functions of the Board as is 
required to effectuate this subsection is 
transferred to the Secretary of Labor. 
The provisions of this section notwith­
standing, decisions made by the National 
War Labor Board in individual cases 
brought before it pursuant to law shall 
not be subject to modification by the Sec­
retary of Labor but shall have the same 
degree of finality as existed prior to the 
issuance of this order.
3. (a) The Retraining and Réemployé 
ment Administration, established by sec­
tion 301 of the War Mobilization and Re­
conversion Act of 1944, and all of its 
functions, officers, employees, records, 
property, and funds are hereby trans­
ferred to the Department of Labor and 
shall be administered under the super­

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and the statutes, 
including Title I of the First War Powers 
Act, 1941, and as President of the United 
States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1 , (a) Except as otherwise provided 
herein, all functions, agencies, officers, 
employees, records, property, and funds 
of the War Manpower Commission, es­
tablished by Executive Order 9139 of 
April 18, 1942, are hereby transferred to 
the Department of Labor and shall be 
administered under the supervision, di­
rection, and control of the Secretary of 
Labor.
(b) All of the functions of the Chair­
man of the War Manpower Commission, 
exclusive of so much thereof as relates 
to the functions of the Procurement and 
Assignment Service transferred by para­
graph 5 of this order, are transferred to 
the Secretary of Labor.
(c) The War Manpower Commission 
is hereby terminated.
(d) In order to maintain the essential 
coordination of public employment serv­
ice and unemployment compensation 
functions and to avoid any necessity for 
establishing duplicate public employ­
ment office facilities, the Department of 
Labor is directed to provide for making 
available to agencies charged with the 
administration of unemployment com­
pensation laws such services, informa­
tion, and facilities by the United States 
Employment Service as the Secretary of 
Labor shall find not inconsistent with 
the purposes of this order. To the extent 
that Federal funds under the jurisdiction 
of the Social Security Board are involved 
in the effectuation of this section, serv­
ices, information, and facilities shall be 
furnished only when, and to the extent 
that the Social Security Board shall 
approve.
2. (a) The National War Labor Board, 
established by Executive Order 9017 of 
January 12, 1942, and all of its func­
tions, officers, employees, records, prop­
erty, and funds are hereby transferred
to the Department of Labor and shall, 
except as otherwise provided in this or­
der, be administered under the super­
vision, direction, and control of the Sec­
retary of Labor.
(b) The National War Labor Board in 
the Department of Labor shall be in all 
respects subject to and governed by such 
policies, consistent with law, as the Sec­
retary of Labor shall prescribe; and so 
much of the functions of the Board as is 
required to effectuate this subsection is 
transferred to the Secretary of Labor. 
The provisions of this section notwith­
standing, decisions made by the National 
War Labor Board in individual cases 
brought before it pursuant to law shall 
not be subject to modification by the Sec­
retary of Labor but shall have the same 
degree of finality as existed prior to the 
issuance of this order.
3. (a) The Retraining and Réemployé 
ment Administration, established by sec­
tion 301 of the War Mobilization and Re­
conversion Act of 1944, and all of its 
functions, officers, employees, records, 
property, and funds are hereby trans­
ferred to the Department of Labor and 
shall be administered under the super­
vision, direction, and control of the Sec­
retary of Labor.
(b) The functions of the Director of 
War Mobilization and Reconversion re­
lating to the Retraining and Reemploy­
ment Administration are hereby trans­
ferred to the Secretary of Labor.
4. (a) The Secretary of Labor may 
perform the functions transferred to him 
by this order through such officials, per­
sons, or agencies and in such manner as 
he shall determine.

partment of Labor. All other functions

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Executive Order No. 9165 of May 19, 1942 "is hereby" revoked (printed 'is hereby revoked' at the end of one line). The order states no effective date, so the revocation was performed on signing, April 18, 1944; the filing date, April 20, 1944, is not used. The command is exhausted by performance and EO 9165 stays revoked. The second paragraph, which begins "This order shall not be deemed to", limits what the revocation terminates and adds no continuing command.

Doc. 44-5654, filed April 20, 1944) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. It revokes EO 9165 of May 19, 1942 (protection of essential facilities from sabotage and other destructive acts) and adds a sentence that the order does not terminate War Department facility security functions or preclude cooperative arrangements with the agencies named in paragraph 3 of EO 9165. The order states no effective date, so the revocation was performed on signing, 1944-04-18, and the order is exhausted by performance; EO 9165 stays revoked as a surviving consequence. The second paragraph is a limit on what the revocation terminates, not a separate command, and is kept within the single scope. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

The machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage (all three marked complete, no scope note) and are recorded as leads, not as independent review. Nothing shows an earlier end of the revocation; no effective-date wording is in the order, so it is read as effective on signing.","independent_command_check":"No independent command: the second paragraph preserves existing War Department functions and arrangements; it creates no direction of its own.","savings_check":"The second paragraph is itself a savings provision for War Department facility security functions and cooperative arrangements; they continue on their own authority, so the savings state is continuing_independent.","scope_check":"One operative scope (EO:9437#whole): the revocation paragraph and the sentence limiting its effect. savings_residuals.reason: The second paragraph says the order "This order shall not be deemed to" terminate any facility security functions of the War Department or preclude cooperative arrangements with the agencies named in paragraph 3 of EO 9165 (the sentence is printed across several lines). Those War Department functions and arrangements rest on their own authority, not on EO 9437, and continue independently of it.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: item 1: The Secretaries of War and the Navy are authorized and directed to permit non-military and non-naval transportation on Army and Navy air transports on foreign routes, on the provisos that follow. The order ended with the whole order by its own terms as amended: EO 9886 (signed August 22, 1947) substituted 'three years and one month' in paragraph 2(c) and added "This order shall cease to be in effect at such time, not later than the expiration of" that period (the sentence runs across several printed lines), as the Secretary of Defense may specifically provide in regulations or orders superseding the order. Three years and one month from October 24, 1944 is November 24, 1947, recorded inclusive (the exclusive reading is that the order ended as November 24 began). If the Secretary of Defense superseded the order earlier, the first end would fall between 1947-08-22 and 1947-11-23; no such regulation or order is held, so 1947-11-24 is the latest date the order permits and the best supported date.

Three years and one month from October 24, 1944 is November 24, 1947, recorded inclusive (the exclusive reading is that the order ended as November 24 began). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: item 2(c): No non-military and non-naval traffic may be carried if a United States civil air carrier can reasonably handle it, and charged traffic other than war-effort and lend-lease traffic is terminated at the end of the stated period from the date of the order, or earlier on a route if the Civil Aeronautics Board certifies that civil carriers can handle it. The order ended with the whole order by its own terms as amended: EO 9886 (signed August 22, 1947) substituted 'three years and one month' in paragraph 2(c) and added "This order shall cease to be in effect at such time, not later than the expiration of" that period (the sentence runs across several printed lines), as the Secretary of Defense may specifically provide in regulations or orders superseding the order. Three years and one month from October 24, 1944 is November 24, 1947, recorded inclusive (the exclusive reading is that the order ended as November 24 began). If the Secretary of Defense superseded the order earlier, the first end would fall between 1947-08-22 and 1947-11-23; no such regulation or order is held, so 1947-11-24 is the latest date the order permits and the best supported date.

WHEREAS at the present stage of the  
war there is a steadily increasing emer­
gency need for air transportation to,  
within, and between war theaters and  
foreign countries for official and civilian  
travel on missions important in the win­
ning of the war, in relief and rehabilita­
tion activities, and in speeding a return  
of peace conditions; and  
WHEREAS this need cannot ade­
quately be met at the present time by

WHEREAS the Air Transport Com­

tend such routes; and

mand and the Naval Air Transport Serv­
ice there will be space on aircraft which  
may not be required for military and  
naval personnel or material in connec­
tion with the war effort but which un­
der existing policies cannot generally be  
made available to traffic of the charac­
ter referred to herein:

authority vested in me by the Constitu­

as President of the United States and

ordered as follows:

tional interest because it will contribute  
directly or indirectly to the war effort,  
or by the State Department, or the War
or Navy Department acting for the State  
Department, as being in the national in­
terest because it will similarly contribute
(i) to relief or rehabilitation activities in

ties, disrupted by the war, that are nec­
essary for the prompt reestablishment

fied as being of such importance as to

research_rationale:
EO 9492 (signed October 24, 1944; F.R. Doc. 44-16439, filed October 25, 1944) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. The order authorizes and directs the Secretaries of War and the Navy to permit non-military and non-naval passengers and cargo on Army and Navy air transports on foreign routes when certified (item 1 with provisos (a) and (b)) and to prescribe regulations containing priority, charge and termination provisions (item 2 with paragraphs (a), (b) and (c)). Paragraph 2(c) originally ended charged traffic 'one year from the date of this order'. Five amendment orders each substituted a longer period in paragraph 2(c), each signed before the then-current period ran out: EO 9629 (1945-09-25, eighteen months), EO 9714 (1946-04-20, two years, and a new section 3), EO 9792 (1946-10-23, two and one-half years), EO 9840 (1947-04-22, two years and eight months) and EO 9867 (1947-06-23, two years and ten months). EO 9886 (1947-08-22) set three years and one month and added a sentence that the order shall cease to be in effect not later than the expiration of that period, earlier if the Secretary of Defense so provides in superseding regulations or orders. No held source shows an earlier superseding issuance, so the first end of every scope is the outer limit, 1947-11-24 (three years and one month from October 24, 1944). The amendments are later events; each amendment continues the clause, amended (owner ruling 2026-10-21). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

The six amendments were read; the dossier chain lists them. The machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage (all three marked complete, no scope note) and are recorded as leads, not as independent review. The Secretary of Defense regulations that EO 9886 allows to supersede the order earlier are not held, so no earlier end is shown.","independent_command_check":"All eight scopes depend on the order as a whole (permission to carry traffic, the regulations directive and the one-year limit) and end together with it; no scope is an independent standing command.","savings_check":"No savings clause in EO 9886 or in the held amendments; no later held text preserves any provision.","scope_check":"Eight scopes in the machine inventory: item 1 with provisos (a), (i) and (b) of item 1, item 2, and paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of item 2. The lead recitals, the contents text printed inside the clause (c) offsets, the signature and the filing line carry no command. Inventory confirmed complete; section 3 added by EO 9714 is a later amendment event, not an original scope."}

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9672
Establishing  the N ational W age S ta­
bilization B oard and T erminating the
N ational W ar L abor B oard
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Constitution and Statutes, in­
cluding Title I of the First War Powers 
Act, 1941, and the Stabilization Act of 
1942, as amended, and as President of 
the United States, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
1. (a) There is hereby established 
within the Department of Labor a Board 
to be known as the National Wage Sta­
bilization Board, hereinafter referred to 
as the Board. The Board shall be com­
posed of six members to be appointed by 
the President (two of whom, including 
the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman, 
shall be representative of the public, two 
representative of employees, and two rep­
resentative of employers), and such addi­
tional members as may, in view of the 
necessities of the business of the Board, 
be appointed from time to time by unan­
imous action of a quorum of the Board 
to serve as alternates representing, re­
spectively, the public, employees, and 
employers.
(b) Six members, equally representa­
tive of the three groups comprising the 
Board, shall constitute a quorum for the 
transaction of business, and the Board 
may act with not more than twelve mem­
bers likewise equally representative of 
such three groups.
(c) Members of the Board (including 
alternates) shall receive actual trans­
portation expenses and other necessary 
expenses, and not to exceed $25 per diem 
in lieu of subsistence, whether or not in 
travel status, on such days as they are 
actually engaged in the performance of 
duties pursuant to this order without 
other compensation from the United 
States.
(d) The Board shall be administered 
as an organizational entity within the 
Department of L^bor and shall be inde­
pendent with respect to its policies, de­
cisions, and control of personnel.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: item 1: Executive Order No. 9017 is amended by increasing the number of public members of the National War Labor Board from four to eight, with not more than four voting on any one matter. The clause continues, amended, as long as the Board exists (owner ruling 2026-10-21). EO 9672 section 4 says of the Board that it "is hereby terminated" (printed 'and the National War Labor Board is hereby terminated.' across lines), with no effective-date wording, so the Board and the enlarged public membership ended on signing, December 31, 1945. Before and after: before the amendment the Board had four public members; after it, eight, until the Board ended.

EO 9535 (signed April 4, 1945; F.R. Doc. 45-5541, filed April 5, 1945) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Item 1 amends EO 9017 of January 12, 1942 (the National War Labor Board) by increasing the public members from four to eight, with not more than four voting on any one matter; item 2 revokes EO 9038 of January 24, 1942 (associate members) and EO 9395-A of November 20, 1943 (alternate public members). The held text then prints a Bureau of Customs regulation (T.D. 51214); it is another document and was not used. Item 2 is a one-time revocation performed on signing, 1945-04-04. Item 1 continues, amended, until its parent ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21); the National War Labor Board ended when EO 9672 (signed December 31, 1945; 11 FR 221) section 4 terminated it, with no effective-date wording, so on 1945-12-31. The whole-order end is the later date. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9672
Establishing  the N ational W age S ta­
bilization B oard and T erminating the
N ational W ar L abor B oard
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Constitution and Statutes, in­
cluding Title I of the First War Powers 
Act, 1941, and the Stabilization Act of 
1942, as amended, and as President of 
the United States, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
1. (a) There is hereby established 
within the Department of Labor a Board 
to be known as the National Wage Sta­
bilization Board, hereinafter referred to 
as the Board. The Board shall be com­
posed of six members to be appointed by 
the President (two of whom, including 
the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman, 
shall be representative of the public, two 
representative of employees, and two rep­
resentative of employers), and such addi­
tional members as may, in view of the 
necessities of the business of the Board, 
be appointed from time to time by unan­
imous action of a quorum of the Board 
to serve as alternates representing, re­
spectively, the public, employees, and 
employers.
(b) Six members, equally representa­
tive of the three groups comprising the 
Board, shall constitute a quorum for the 
transaction of business, and the Board 
may act with not more than twelve mem­
bers likewise equally representative of 
such three groups.
(c) Members of the Board (including 
alternates) shall receive actual trans­
portation expenses and other necessary 
expenses, and not to exceed $25 per diem 
in lieu of subsistence, whether or not in 
travel status, on such days as they are 
actually engaged in the performance of 
duties pursuant to this order without 
other compensation from the United 
States.
(d) The Board shall be administered 
as an organizational entity within the 
Department of L^bor and shall be inde­
pendent with respect to its policies, de­
cisions, and control of personnel.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9672
Establishing  the N ational W age S ta­
bilization B oard and T erminating the
N ational W ar L abor B oard
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Constitution and Statutes, in­
cluding Title I of the First War Powers 
Act, 1941, and the Stabilization Act of 
1942, as amended, and as President of 
the United States, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
1. (a) There is hereby established 
within the Department of Labor a Board 
to be known as the National Wage Sta­
bilization Board, hereinafter referred to 
as the Board. The Board shall be com­
posed of six members to be appointed by 
the President (two of whom, including 
the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman, 
shall be representative of the public, two 
representative of employees, and two rep­
resentative of employers), and such addi­
tional members as may, in view of the 
necessities of the business of the Board, 
be appointed from time to time by unan­
imous action of a quorum of the Board 
to serve as alternates representing, re­
spectively, the public, employees, and 
employers.
(b) Six members, equally representa­
tive of the three groups comprising the 
Board, shall constitute a quorum for the 
transaction of business, and the Board 
may act with not more than twelve mem­
bers likewise equally representative of 
such three groups.
(c) Members of the Board (including 
alternates) shall receive actual trans­
portation expenses and other necessary 
expenses, and not to exceed $25 per diem 
in lieu of subsistence, whether or not in 
travel status, on such days as they are 
actually engaged in the performance of 
duties pursuant to this order without 
other compensation from the United 
States.
(d) The Board shall be administered 
as an organizational entity within the 
Department of L^bor and shall be inde­
pendent with respect to its policies, de­
cisions, and control of personnel.

uty Petroleum Administrator may deter­

research_rationale:
EO 9566 (signed June 5, 1945; F.R. Doc. 45-9823, filed June 6, 1945) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Its only operative text is one paragraph, issued under section 4 of the Air Commerce Act of 1926, revoking EO 9090 of March 6, 1942 (airspace reservation over portions of Ulster and Dutchess Counties, New York). The held page text goes on to print War Food Order 66 Amendment 10 and other regulations; the machine inventory wrongly included the War Food Order amendment as scopes, so the inventory is corrected by override to the single paragraph. The revocation states no effective date and was performed on signing, 1945-06-05; EO 9090 stays revoked as a surviving consequence. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

Nothing shows an earlier end or a postponement of the revocation; the order states no effective date.","independent_command_check":"No independent command: one revocation, performed on signing.","savings_check":"No savings clause in EO 9566; the revocation's result is an accrued effect and nothing continues as a command.","scope_check":"Inventory corrected to one scope (EO:9566#whole) by override over offsets 3768-4062 of the held text; the other three machine scopes are text of War Food Order 66 Amendment 10, not of this order. savings_residuals.reason: EO 9566 has no savings, transfer or exemption language. The War Food Order savings sentence on the same page belongs to a different document.

SU B PA R T  1945
Pursuant to the provisions of section 
302 of the Agricultural Adjustment Act 
of 1938, as amended (52 Stat. 43; 7 U.S.C. 
1940 ed., 1302), Commodity Credit Cor­
poration has authorized the making of 
loans on cover crop and hay and pasture 
seed, in accordance with the regulations 
in this part (1945 C.C.C. Cover Crop and 
Hay and Pasture Seed Bulletin I, as 
amended), §  267.15, Eligible seed  is 
amended to read as follows:
110 F.R. 2491.
§  267.15 Eligible seed. Any seed spec­
ified in the attached schedule of loan 
rates, harvested in 1945, stored in a ware­
house which is approved by Commodity 
Credit Corporation and which has exe­
cuted a Seed Cleaning and Storage 
Agreement on C.C.C. Seed Form A, which 
seed complies with the other provisions 
of this bulletin, which is cleaned or can 
be cleaned to meet the specifications as 
shown in the schedule of loan rates, and 
which will comply with the Federal Seed 
Law and the State seed law of the State 
where the seed is produced, is eligible as 
security for a loan, provided it does not 
contain seed of White Top, Canada This­
tle, Dodder, Quackgrass, Johnson Grass, 
Bindweed, Russian Knapweed, Perennial 
Sow Thistle, or Leafy Spurge, singly or 
combined in excess of 45 seeds per pound.
Dated: July 17, 1945.
[ seal ] C. C. F arrington ,
Vice President.
[F. R. Doc. 45-15013; Filed, Aug. 14, 1945;
11:05 a. m.]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Executive Order No. 9528 of March 2, 1945, providing for a change in the order of succession of officers to act as Secretary of the Navy, "is hereby revoked". The order states no effective date, so the revocation was performed on signing, August 13, 1945; the filing date, August 14, 1945, and the Federal Register issue date, August 15, 1945, are not used. The command is exhausted by performance and EO 9528 stays revoked.

research_rationale:
EO 9596 (signed August 13, 1945; F.R. Doc. 45-15025, filed August 14, 1945) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Under Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941 and other statutes it revokes EO 9528 of March 2, 1945, which changed the order of succession of officers to act as Secretary of the Navy. The held page text goes on to print Department of Agriculture regulations; they are other documents and were not used. The order states no effective date, so the one-time revocation was performed on signing, 1945-08-13; EO 9528 stays revoked as a surviving consequence. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

research_rationale:
EO 9601 (signed August 21, 1945; F.R. Doc. 45-15487, filed August 21, 1945) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. It revokes EO 9240, as amended, entitled Regulations Relating to Overtime Wage Compensation, effective as of the date of the order. The held page text goes on to print other material after the filing line; it was not used. The revocation is a one-time command performed on 1945-08-21; EO 9240 stays revoked as a surviving consequence. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Paragraph 4 of Executive Order No. 9279 of December 5, 1942, "be, and it is hereby, revoked", in order to permit voluntary enlistments in the armed forces. The order states no effective date, so the revocation was performed on signing, August 29, 1945. The command is exhausted by performance and paragraph 4 of EO 9279 stays revoked as a surviving consequence.

research_rationale:
EO 9605 (signed August 29, 1945) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. It revokes paragraph 4 of EO 9279 of December 5, 1942 so as to permit voluntary enlistments in the armed forces. The held text ends at the signature date; the Federal Register page text before and after (a contents column) was not used. The order states no effective date, so the one-time revocation was performed on signing, 1945-08-29; paragraph 4 of EO 9279 stays revoked as a surviving consequence. The dossier's missing list names Public Law 89-554 as an acting identity absent from the census; no held text of that act that names EO 9605 or EO 9279 was found, and under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments a statute that does not name the target does not end it. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: "I hereby adopt and rat" (the verb is hyphenated across two printed lines) the capture made as prize by Captain J. F. Devlin of the War Shipping Administration in July 1945 of the German motor vessel Caribia and her contents. The order states no effective date, so the adoption was performed on signing, August 29, 1945. The act is exhausted by performance and the ratified capture stands as a surviving consequence.

research_rationale:
EO 9606 (signed August 29, 1945; F.R. Doc. 45-16187, filed August 29, 1945) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Under section 4613 of the Revised Statutes and the act of August 18, 1942, as amended, the President adopts and ratifies the capture as prize, by Captain J. F. Devlin of the War Shipping Administration in July 1945, of the German motor vessel Caribia with her equipment and the property on board. The held text then prints a Commodity Credit Corporation regulation; it is another document and was not used. The adoption is a one-time act performed on signing, 1945-08-29; the ratified capture stands as a surviving consequence. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

The machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage (all three marked complete, no scope note) and are recorded as leads, not as independent review. Nothing shows that the adoption was withdrawn or limited before or after 1945-08-29.","independent_command_check":"No independent command: a single act of adoption and ratification.","savings_check":"No savings clause.
